question_interpretation: Who is covered by the Part 111 dietary supplement CGMP rule (scope/applicability), including any exclusion.

issues.detail: J omits the two express inclusions in 111.1(a): (1) a dietary supplement you manufacture that is packaged or labeled by another person, and (2) dietary supplements imported or offered for import into any State/territory, DC or Puerto Rico.

J's 'excludes certain retailers/holders' overstates and blurs 111.1(b): the exclusion covers only the requirements pertaining to HOLDING, only for holding at a retail establishment for the sole purpose of direct retail sale to individual consumers, and a retail establishment expressly does not include a warehouse or other storage facility for a retailer or one that sells directly to consumers. Retailers are not excluded from the part as a whole.
'includes those who hold for distribution' is not text of 111.1; holding is covered generally by 111.1(a) ('hold a dietary supplement'). Harmless but not a distinct element.

explanation: 111.1 is the governing section and the core of J (manufacture, package, label or hold) is correct. However J omits the 111.1(a)(1)-(2) inclusions (contract-packaged/labeled product; imports) and describes the 111.1(b) exclusion too loosely: it exempts only holding requirements for retail-establishment holding for direct retail sale, and warehouses are carved back in. A key this vague would credit an answer that says retailers are outside Part 111 altogether.
proposed_corrected_answer: You are subject to Part 111 if you manufacture, package, label, or hold a dietary supplement, including (1) a dietary supplement you manufacture but that is packaged or labeled by another person and (2) a dietary supplement imported or offered for import into any State or territory, DC or Puerto Rico (111.1(a)). Exception (111.1(b)): the requirements pertaining to holding do not apply to holding at a retail establishment for the sole purpose of direct retail sale to individual consumers; a retail establishment does not include a warehouse or other storage facility for a retailer or one that sells directly to individual consumers.

question_interpretation: What Part 111 requires for the water supply of a dietary supplement facility.

issues.detail: G cites 21 CFR 111.16, which only requires written procedures for cleaning the physical plant and for pest control. The water supply requirement is 111.15(e); related requirements are 111.23(c) (records showing water that may become a component meets 111.15(e)(2)), 111.365(c) (manufacturing operations precaution), and plumbing 111.15(f).

J says water that contacts components/product or contact surfaces 'must be safe and sanitary quality'. The text assigns the 'safe and sanitary' standard (with suitable temperature and pressure) to water used where it does NOT become a component (111.15(e)(1)). Water that may become a component — e.g., water that contacts components, dietary supplements, or contact surfaces — must at a minimum comply with applicable Federal, State, and local requirements and not contaminate the dietary supplement (111.15(e)(2)).
J omits the 111.23(c) record requirement and the two-tier structure of 111.15(e).

explanation: 111.16 is the Subpart C written-procedures section and does not mention water. The governing provision is 111.15(e), and J misstates which standard applies to contact water: contact water is treated as water that may become a component and must comply with applicable Federal, State and local requirements and not contaminate the product, with records under 111.23(c).
proposed_corrected_answer: 111.15(e)(1): provide water that is safe and sanitary, at suitable temperatures, and under pressure as needed, for all uses where water does not become a component of the dietary supplement. 111.15(e)(2): water used in a manner such that it may become a component (e.g., water that contacts components, dietary supplements, or any contact surface) must, at a minimum, comply with applicable Federal, State, and local requirements and not contaminate the dietary supplement. 111.23(c): make and keep records showing that such water meets 111.15(e)(2). Related: plumbing must carry sufficient water and prevent backflow/cross-connection (111.15(f)); manufacturing operations must use such water (111.365(c)).

question_interpretation: When a finished batch fails an identity (product) specification, what Part 111 requires the firm to do and who decides disposition.

issues.detail: G omits 111.77(a) — the section that directly answers 'what must you do if established specifications are not met': for 111.70(e) product specifications not met, QC personnel must reject the dietary supplement unless they approve a treatment, in-process adjustment, or reprocessing that will ensure quality, and no finished batch may be released unless it complies with 111.123(b).

G omits 111.113 (QC must conduct a material review and make a disposition decision when a 111.70 specification is not met; reject unless QC approves treatment/adjustment/reprocessing as permitted by 111.77; document at time of performance) and 111.123(b)(2) (QC must not approve and release any batch, including a reprocessed batch, that does not meet all 111.70(e) product specifications).

J does not state the default outcome (rejection) or the release prohibition, and omits documentation of the material review/disposition and investigation in the batch production record (111.113(c), 111.140(b)(3)) and corrective action plans (111.75(i)).

Distinguish component identity failures: a component that fails its 111.70(b)(1) identity specification must be rejected and not used (111.77(b)), and any batch containing such a component cannot be released (111.123(b)(1)).

explanation: The cited 111.87 (QC personnel decide) and 111.90 (reprocessing conditions) are correct and answer 'who', but the key omits 111.77(a), the provision that tells the firm what to do when a specification is not met, plus 111.113 and 111.123(b). A fully correct answer centered on 111.77/111.113/111.123(b) would cite sections outside the key.
proposed_corrected_answer: A finished batch's identity specification is a 111.70(e) product specification; you must determine whether it is met (111.73, 111.75(c)). If it is not met, quality control personnel must conduct a material review and make a disposition decision (111.87, 111.113(a)(1)) and must reject the batch unless they approve a reprocessing (or treatment/in-process adjustment) that will ensure quality and correct packaging/labeling (111.77(a), 111.113(b)(2)). Reprocessing requires a QC material review and disposition decision based on a scientifically valid reason, must be permitted by 111.77, and the reprocessed batch must be approved by QC and comply with 111.123(b) before release (111.90). QC must not release any batch, including a reprocessed batch, that does not meet all product specifications (111.123(b)(2)). The material review and disposition must be documented at the time of performance, including the investigation and corrective/preventive action, in the batch production record (111.113(c), 111.140(b)(3)); corrective action plans for unmet specifications are required (111.75(i)).

question_interpretation: Which representative samples Part 111 requires, and the requirements for reserve samples.

issues.detail: J lists representative samples of components, packaging, labels, in-process and finished batch but omits 111.80(d) (each unique shipment/lot of product received for packaging or labeling) and 111.80(e) (each lot of packaged and labeled dietary supplements).

J's 'storage conditions' element is governed by 111.465(a)(1) (hold under conditions consistent with product labels or, if none, ordinary storage conditions), which G does not cite; 111.83 only specifies the container-closure system.

J omits that reserve samples must be collected from each lot of packaged and labeled dietary supplements distributed (111.83(a)) and identified with the batch, lot, or control number (111.83(b)(2)); and does not state the actual values (at least twice the quantity needed for all tests; 1 year past shelf life or 2 years from distribution of the last batch).

explanation: 111.80 and 111.83 are the right primary sections, but J omits two of the five representative-sample categories, and its storage-conditions element comes from 111.465 (not cited). Key numeric values are not stated in J, so the key cannot check them.
proposed_corrected_answer: 111.80: collect representative samples of (a) each unique lot of components, packaging and labels (and of each unique shipment and lot within it when received from a supplier); (b) in-process materials for each batch at control points in the master manufacturing record; (c) a subset of finished batches identified through a sound statistical sampling plan (or every finished batch) before release; (d) each unique shipment and lot of product received for packaging or labeling; (e) each lot of packaged and labeled dietary supplements. 111.83: collect and hold reserve samples of each lot of packaged and labeled dietary supplements you distribute; held in the same container-closure system as distributed (or one with essentially the same protective characteristics); identified with batch, lot or control number; retained 1 year past the shelf-life date (if used) or 2 years from distribution of the last associated batch; at least twice the quantity necessary for all tests/examinations to determine whether product specifications are met. 111.465: hold reserve samples to protect against contamination and deterioration, under conditions consistent with product labels or, if none, ordinary storage conditions. QC ensures collection (111.105(f)-(g)).

question_interpretation: What Part 111 requires quality control personnel to do (QC duties).

issues.detail: The question asks what QC must do 'under Part 111', but G cites only 111.105. J's elements 'perform material review and disposition' and 'approve reprocessing' come from 111.87, 111.113, 111.120(c)-(d), 111.123(a)(4)-(5) and 111.130, and 'review records' from 111.123(a)(2), 111.127(c), 111.117(b)-(c); none is in 111.105 itself.

J omits 111.105 duties: reviewing/approving supplier-qualification and specification-basis documentation (b)-(e), ensuring representative samples are collected (f), ensuring reserve samples are collected and held (g), and determining whether all 111.70(a) specifications are met (h); and the core release function (approving and releasing, or rejecting, each finished batch, 111.123(a)(8)), with the 111.123(b) release prohibitions.
QC must document review/approval/rejection at the time of performance with date and signature (111.140(b)(2)).

explanation: 111.105 is the central section and J's 'approve/reject' (deviations and modifications) element is supported by 111.105(a), but other J elements come from sections not in G, and J omits several 111.105 duties and the batch release decision. The key is incomplete in both citation and content.
proposed_corrected_answer: 111.105: QC personnel must ensure operations ensure quality and correct packaging/labeling per the master manufacturing record, including (a) approving or rejecting all processes, specifications, written procedures, controls, tests and examinations, and deviations from or modifications to them, that may affect identity, purity, strength or composition; (b)-(e) reviewing and approving supplier-qualification documentation and the documented bases for in-process, finished-batch and exempted specifications; (f) ensuring required representative samples are collected; (g) ensuring reserve samples are collected and held; (h) determining whether all 111.70(a) specifications are met; (i) other Subpart F operations. These include: conducting all material reviews and disposition decisions (111.87, 111.113); laboratory control review (111.110); equipment/calibration review (111.117); approving and releasing components, packaging and labels from quarantine (111.120); reviewing and approving MMRs and batch records, approving or rejecting reprocessing, and approving and releasing or rejecting each finished batch, never releasing batches that fail 111.123(b) (111.123); packaging/labeling, returned-product and complaint duties (111.127, 111.130, 111.135); documenting each review at the time of performance with date and signature (111.140(b)(2)).
